The blocking dependence is a loop-carried RAW on array `v`: iteration i reads `v[kv[i]]` (line 6) which was written by an earlier iteration j < i at line 7 (where `jv[j] == kv[i]`). This value flows through the array over multiple iterations.

**Solution:** Split the original loop into two sequential sub-passes:
1. First pass: execute all writes to `v` (line 7 for all i)
2. Second pass: execute all reads from `v` and updates to `u` (line 6 for all i)

This breaks the loop-carried dependence within each individual loop. Each sub-loop should now have no loop-carried dependencies through `v`, enabling DiscoPoP to detect them as Do-All parallelizable.

**Bounds:** Both loops keep the same iteration range `i=1` to `i < LEN_1D` (31999 iterations), as splitting doesn't change which iterations execute—only their order between the two statements.
